newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge down ahead of holidays.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge down ahead of holidays.

text.p: Shares in regional oil company Tatneft rose sharply on news of an ADR placement, while national grid operator UES fell, but dealers said there was no clear trend in a market already winding down for the holidays.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares fell by 0.06 percent to 185.14 on $11.59 million in volume.
Anton Kudryashov, head of equity trading at Renaissance Capital, said the market was resistant to any stimulus.
"There is a pre-holiday apathy on the market and even if the International Monetary Fund decides to pay us the next tranche, it will not move prices anywhere," he said.
UES fell to $0.0816 from $0.0828 at Friday's close.

Reports from UES that its pre-tax profit on deliveries in the first nine months of 1996 rose to 659.72 billion roubles from 370.70 billion a year earlier, prevented the share from falling further, said Alexei Dolgikh, chief trader at Troika Dialog.
A trader from IK Aton said heavy supply in UES shares prompted the fall.
Tatneft rose to $45.25 from $42.10 on Friday, dragged up by last week's private placement of American Depositary Shares at $45.00 a share, Dolgikh said.
"The share rose a bit, but there was no global rise," he said.
The Aton trader said demand was strongest for second-tier shares, including oil ones, where the fall was smaller than in other issues.

Gazprom fell to $0.309 from $0.312, Nizhnevartovskneftegaz rose to $8.10 from $7.05 on December 5 close when it was last traded, Rostelekom edged down to $2.29 from $2.30 and Norilsk Nickel was $5.25 after $5.17.
